course_name_original: ENGLISH AND COMMUNICATION SKILLS FOR ENGINEERING
course_name_en: English and Communication Skills for Engineering
prerequisites: B1 CEFR level general English proficiency

learning_outcomes.text: Achieve English language proficiency at B2 CEFR level.
Communicate more confidently and effectively in international academic and workplace contexts.
Choose and use the technical jargon appropriate to the industrial and construction engineering sectors.
Collaborate effectively in teams to create or review documents.
Present their own projects in front of a variety of audiences.
Interact effectively on a range of topics within the engineering field of choice, substantiate opinions with evidence, and negotiate them with colleagues.
Find answers to specific questions in texts on engineering topics in a range of media.
Understand oral texts and summarize and/or paraphrase written texts about technical topics, and use the conventions of formal correspondence.

syllabus_topics: English language proficiency in all four skills (speaking, listening, reading, writing) at B2 CEFR level, adapted to language and communication needs of engineers (GELS Framework)
Communication skills in industrial, governmental, and applied research environments
Topics common to all kinds of engineering (civil, electrical, electronic, and mechanical), such as processes, measurements, and components
Specialist English for engineers in the international market
Authentic activities: reporting on technical problems and suggesting solutions
Communicating technical ideas to specialist as well as non-specialist audiences

assessment_methods.method: 10 minute oral presentation of a project and/or process relevant to the individual student's specialization

assessment_rules: The exam consists of an online multiple choice test with items of the type practiced in class, followed by a 10 minute oral presentation of one of the projects and/or processes relevant to the individual student's specialisation of choice. For the English for Engineering module (3 CFU), the assessment is an online multiple choice test followed by a brief oral presentation of one of the activities introduced during the course. For the English Language Lab module (3 CFU), the assessment is a 10 minute oral presentation of one of the projects and/or processes relevant to the individual student's specialisation of choice. By successfully passing the English for Engineering exam, students can enrol in an engineering Master's degree taught entirely in English without further language tests.
bibliography: Ibbotson, Mark (2009) Professional English in Use: Engineering. With Answers. Series: Technical English for Professionals, B1-B2, Cambridge, Cambridge University Press
